builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
summary: Replaces naive sequential application of single-task editing methods (e.g., null-space-constrained editors such as MEMIT-style updates) with conflict-aware task ordering plus dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the common null space. Costs an additional ordering step, a conflict-index computation, and per-edit low-rank factors rather than single updates; editing remains cheap relative to fine-tuning but adds implementation complexity. Fails when task Jacobians share almost no null space so that even expanded low-rank directions cannot accommodate conflict-free updates, and benefits may not transfer to backbones or domains beyond the five tested.
rationale: Multi-task sequential editing is a niche production need, the abstract gives no numeric gain, and validation is confined to three backbones, so the reader should track it rather than adopt it.
technique: Conflict-aware sequential model editing with low-rank null-space expansion

claims.statement: Replaces naive sequential application of single-task editing methods (e.g., null-space-constrained editors such as MEMIT-style updates) with conflict-aware task ordering plus dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the common null space. Costs an additional ordering step, a conflict-index computation, and per-edit low-rank factors rather than single updates; editing remains cheap relative to fine-tuning but adds implementation complexity. Fails when task Jacobians share almost no null space so that even expanded low-rank directions cannot accommodate conflict-free updates, and benefits may not transfer to backbones or domains beyond the five tested.

Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities across five domains and three backbones; no multiplicative factor reported.
